name: Mudhoney
label: Sub Pop
lede: Named after a Russ Meyer movie none of them had seen, built from two fuzz pedals and a joke, and still standing long after the bigger Seattle bands they helped make possible.

eras.title: Two fuzz pedals and a dirty movie title
eras.text: Green River fell apart on Halloween 1987, and Mark Arm and Steve Turner went looking for something dumber, louder and more fun. With Melvins bassist Matt Lukin and drummer Dan Peters, they made the two Sub Pop records that sold the world on the Seattle sound before anyone had a name for it.

years.h: Mudhoney's first practice: Arm, Turner, Lukin and Peters
years.p: Mark Arm and Steve Turner, fresh out of [[Green River|78f56916-fe11-4110-8f10-d553ddf8de7b]], start practicing with ex-[[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]] bassist Matt Lukin and [[Bundle of Hiss|aaa673a8-af81-4140-8cb8-800406c1eace]] drummer Dan Peters on New Year's Day.
years.xp: The name comes from Russ Meyer's 1965 film Mudhoney. According to the band's own history, none of them had actually seen it when they took the name.

years.h: First Mudhoney show: opening for Das Damen at the Vogue
years.p: Mudhoney play their first gig at the Vogue in Seattle, as support for the New York band [[Das Damen|b3f7feae-06fc-4281-9919-f662c1a86287]], less than four months after their first practice.

years.h: Touch Me I'm Sick: Mudhoney's first single
years.p: Sub Pop issues Touch Me I'm Sick backed with Sweet Young Thing Ain't Sweet No More, recorded with [[Jack Endino|d06cca33-9167-4049-b5ce-6a6aeff60a8d]]. It becomes the template for a whole scene's guitar sound.
years.xp: Sub Pop's Bruce Pavitt first heard Mudhoney on a boombox recording, according to Wikipedia, and sent them to Endino at Reciprocal Recording. The single's blown-out Big Muff tone and Arm's yelp set the bar for every Seattle band that followed.

years.h: Superfuzz Bigmuff: an EP named after two pedals
years.p: Mudhoney's six-song debut EP takes its title from Steve Turner's and Mark Arm's fuzz boxes, the Univox Super-Fuzz and Electro-Harmonix Big Muff.
years.xp:
[[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] later listed Superfuzz Bigmuff among his favorite albums in his journal. Sub Pop reissued it in 2008 as a deluxe set with the original running order, the early singles, demos and 1988 live tapes.

Critic Jay Hinman summed up the era: there was Mudhoney, and then there was everybody else.

years.h: Mudhoney and [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] cover each other on one split single
years.p: On a Sub Pop split 7-inch, Sonic Youth cover Mudhoney's Touch Me I'm Sick and Mudhoney cover Sonic Youth's Halloween.
years.xp: Sonic Youth were Mudhoney's biggest early champions and took them on tour through the West Coast, the Southwest and the UK. Mark Arm has said the Sonic Youth connection gave Mudhoney instant credibility in Britain.

eras.title: Big in Britain, broke at home
eras.text: The UK press fell for Mudhoney before America did, and a tour behind Sonic Youth turned them into the headliners of Sub Pop's traveling circus. By 1991 they had a best-selling Sub Pop album and a label that, they said, couldn't pay them for it.

years.h: Mudhoney tour Europe as [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]]'s support act
years.p: Mudhoney's first European trip is as openers for Sonic Youth. In May they return to the UK for a show with some 150 press guests on the list.

years.h: Steve Turner hurts his hand on a car antenna in Nijmegen
years.p: At a chaotic show in Nijmegen, Netherlands, Steve Turner injures his hand on a car antenna, according to the band's fan history. Mudhoney finish the tour anyway.

years.h: Lamefest: Mudhoney top a Sub Pop bill over [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] and [[Tad|867d3fb7-9cd1-47a4-a8f0-de29cdca2004]]
years.p: Sub Pop's Lamefest at Seattle's Moore Theatre puts Mudhoney, Tad and Nirvana on one stage. Bruce Pavitt later called it the turning point for the Seattle scene.

years.h: Mudhoney: the first full-length
years.p: Mudhoney's self-titled debut album comes out on Sub Pop, the first 3,000 copies with a poster, according to the band's fan history.

years.h: Lamefest UK: Mudhoney headline the London Astoria over Tad and Nirvana
years.p: Sub Pop flies the British press to the Astoria on Charing Cross Road. Nirvana open after losing a coin toss; Mudhoney close the night.
years.xp: Pavitt called it Sub Pop's biggest press opportunity ever, with Mudhoney and Nirvana playing in front of the entire British music press. [[Dan Peters|3402566b-20dc-47f1-973b-2af1dedae702]] watched Nirvana fight broken strings and later admitted he'd sat there thinking the set was a disaster.

years.h: Mudhoney's first tour of Australia
years.p: Mudhoney head to Australia for the first time, the start of a long bond with the country that later gives them Australian bassist [[Guy Maddison|81e68e3f-23e1-432a-bdc0-112df4ed728e]].

years.h: Dan Peters drums for [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] on Sliver
years.p: Between Nirvana drummers, [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] and [[Krist Novoselic|ac05e29f-0561-4445-bb26-5562d2389531]] borrow Mudhoney's Dan Peters. He plays on the single Sliver before Nirvana settle on [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]].

years.h: Every Good Boy Deserves Fudge, cut on eight tracks
years.p: Recorded cheaply at [[Conrad Uno|883e716f-9299-426c-9d43-71ca6cb070ba]]'s Egg Studios, Mudhoney's second album does well enough to bring the major labels calling.
years.xp: Sub Pop celebrated the album's 30th anniversary in 2021 with a remastered deluxe edition, adding unreleased songs, demos and restored videos.

eras.title: Reprise, heroin and the backlash
eras.text: Mudhoney took a major-label deal as the scene they'd seeded went global and curdled. Mark Arm nearly died of an overdose, Kurt Cobain did die, and the British press that had crowned them turned on them for still being around.

q: The company didn't seem to give a shit or have a clue.
years.h: Mudhoney leave Sub Pop over unpaid royalties
years.p: Mudhoney split from Sub Pop in a dispute over royalties and accounting on Every Good Boy Deserves Fudge, and sign with Warner Bros. subsidiary Reprise after talks with Epic fall through.
years.xp:
According to the band's history, Mark Arm said Sub Pop had been holding back royalties to fund other projects, and the two sides disagreed on how many copies of the album had actually sold.

The split didn't last forever. Mudhoney came back to Sub Pop in 2002, and Arm ended up running the label's warehouse.

years.h: Mudhoney mock the Seattle hype on the Singles soundtrack
years.p: Mudhoney's contribution to Cameron Crowe's Singles soundtrack is Overblown, a song that takes aim at the grunge gold rush the film was cashing in on.

years.h: Piece of Cake: Mudhoney's major-label debut
years.p: Mudhoney's first Reprise album. Steve Turner later called its songs half-baked.

q: If I was alone, I would have been dead for sure.
years.h: Kurt Cobain helps save Mark Arm from a heroin overdose
years.p: On New Year's Eve, Mark Arm overdoses on heroin in Kurt Cobain and Courtney Love's room at Seattle's Inn at the Market. Cobain and [[Supersuckers|6fa09822-bbe4-4ff8-901d-4a39a4dd82e9]] guitarist Ron Heathman take turns giving him CPR until paramedics arrive.
years.xp: The story is told in Mark Yarm's grunge oral history Everybody Loves Our Town. Arm says he'd decided he wasn't high enough and went back for more; Heathman recalled Arm turning blue while he and Cobain traded CPR, and Courtney Love worrying about what the media would say.

years.h: Five Dollar Bob's Mock Cooter Stew EP on Reprise
years.p: A stopgap EP between Mudhoney's first two Reprise albums.

years.h: Mudhoney tour the Pacific Rim with [[Pearl Jam|83b9cbe7-9857-49e2-ab8e-b57b01038103]]
years.p: Mudhoney spend February and March touring the Pacific Rim with Pearl Jam, the band their old [[Green River|78f56916-fe11-4110-8f10-d553ddf8de7b]] mates [[Jeff Ament|2781b946-104c-47d3-a573-2eade82f68cd]] and [[Stone Gossard|ca7e6e03-4973-45ef-8833-98774a2d4138]] formed.

years.h: My Brother the Cow meets the post-Cobain backlash
years.p: Released eleven months after Kurt Cobain's death, Mudhoney's third Reprise album gets savaged in Britain. Steve Turner said the English press were angry Mudhoney were still around.
years.xp: Not everyone agreed. People told readers to leave the brooding anthems to Pearl Jam, because Mudhoney delivered pure grunge.

years.h: Mudhoney play Poisoned Water in the Chris Farley movie Black Sheep
years.p: Mudhoney turn up as the band at an MTV concert in Black Sheep, the Chris Farley and David Spade comedy.

years.h: Tomorrow Hit Today, produced by Jim Dickinson
years.p: Mudhoney's last Reprise album leans into the blues with Memphis producer Jim Dickinson, who had worked with [[The Rolling Stones|b071f9fa-14b0-4217-8e97-eb41da73f598]]. It was recorded across three cities.

eras.title: Lukin picks up a hammer
eras.text: Matt Lukin quit, Reprise let Mudhoney go, and for a while the band looked finished. Instead they came home to Sub Pop with an Australian bassist and made some of their angriest records.

years.h: Matt Lukin quits Mudhoney to work as a carpenter
years.p: After a long spring world tour, Matt Lukin leaves Mudhoney, having lost his taste for touring. Reprise ends the band's contract soon after.

years.h: Arm, Turner and Peters become the New Strychnines
years.p: Mark Arm, Steve Turner and Dan Peters regroup in April and in May play a [[The Sonics|16346cf4-4d2b-40ec-8393-0fc7296d92fe]] tribute as the New Strychnines with [[Scott McCaughey|90626a1d-dd4d-41eb-ab4b-b5799a81d9a7]].

years.h: Matt Lukin rejoins Mudhoney for one last tour
years.p: Matt Lukin comes back for a run of dates from December 2000 into January 2001, then leaves for good.

years.h: Australian bassist Guy Maddison joins Mudhoney
years.p: [[Guy Maddison|81e68e3f-23e1-432a-bdc0-112df4ed728e]], from [[Lubricated Goat|43034f79-d08f-49e3-a9f0-54b9b6a28508]] and Mark Arm's side band Bloodloss, becomes Mudhoney's bass player.

years.h: Since We've Become Translucent: back on Sub Pop
years.p: Mudhoney's first album with Guy Maddison, and their return to the label that started them.

years.h: Mark Arm sings for the [[MC5|08b736bb-1c82-40b4-8b0b-49e2182a067a]]
years.p: Mark Arm tours with the surviving MC5 members, standing in for their late singer Rob Tyner.

years.h: Under a Billion Suns and Hard-On for War
years.p: Mudhoney's Iraq War-era album includes Hard-On for War, first cut in 2003 for the Buddyhead comp Gimmer Skelter. The same year Mudhoney curate a UK All Tomorrow's Parties.

years.h: Sub Pop turns 20 and Arm and Turner play in [[Green River|78f56916-fe11-4110-8f10-d553ddf8de7b]] again
years.p: At Sub Pop's 20th anniversary party at Marymoor Park near Seattle, Mark Arm and Steve Turner reunite with their old Green River bandmates, [[Pearl Jam|83b9cbe7-9857-49e2-ab8e-b57b01038103]]'s Jeff Ament and Stone Gossard among them.

years.h: The Lucky Ones, produced by Tucker Martine
years.p: Mudhoney cut a raw, fast album with Tucker Martine the same year Sub Pop reissues a deluxe Superfuzz Bigmuff.

eras.title: Still here, still annoyed
eras.text: Mudhoney outlasted the scene, the major labels and most of their peers. They play their old records in full, open for the Green River kids who became Pearl Jam, and keep putting out sharp, funny records on Sub Pop.

years.h: Mudhoney play Superfuzz Bigmuff in full at ATP New York
years.p: At All Tomorrow's Parties in Monticello, New York, Mudhoney perform their 1988 EP from start to finish.

years.h: Mudhoney open Pearl Jam's 20th anniversary tour
years.p: Mudhoney support [[Pearl Jam|83b9cbe7-9857-49e2-ab8e-b57b01038103]] on the PJ20 dates, Mark Arm and Steve Turner opening for their old Green River bandmates Jeff Ament and Stone Gossard.

yt: I'm Now: The Story of Mudhoney
years.h: I'm Now: The Story of Mudhoney documentary
years.p: A feature-length documentary tells Mudhoney's story with the band and their Seattle peers.

years.h: Vanishing Point, Mudhoney's 25th-anniversary album
years.p: Mudhoney mark 25 years with their ninth studio album on Sub Pop.

years.h: Digital Garbage: Mudhoney's tenth album
years.p: Mudhoney's tenth studio album, and their fifth since coming home to Sub Pop.

years.h: Plastic Eternity, Mudhoney's eleventh album
years.p: Mudhoney's first album in five years comes out on Sub Pop, 35 years after Touch Me I'm Sick.
